layers.basics: The DFT turns N samples into N frequency values; it is what computers calculate.
layers.deeper: DTFT is continuous in frequency and periodic; DFT samples it at N points. Circular convolution.
layers.expert: X[k]=Σx[n]e^{−j2πkn/N}; zero-padding interpolates the spectrum, it does not improve resolution; leakage unless periods fit exactly.

title: Fast Fourier transform
summary: DFT in N log N operations.

layers.basics: The FFT computes the DFT far faster by reusing partial results.
layers.deeper: Radix-2 butterflies halve the problem repeatedly; makes real-time spectrum analysis and OFDM feasible.
layers.expert: Cooley–Tukey: O(N log₂N) vs O(N²); N=1024 saves ~100×; real-FFT tricks; Bluestein for prime N.

layers.basics: FIR filters average recent samples with chosen weights; always stable and can have perfect linear phase.
layers.deeper: Windowing a sinc impulse response, or Parks–McClellan optimisation, designs them.
layers.expert: y[n]=Σb_k x[n−k]; linear phase if symmetric; order estimate N≈(−20log√(δ₁δ₂)−13)/(14.6Δf).

layers.basics: IIR filters reuse past outputs, giving sharp responses with few coefficients but risking instability.
layers.deeper: Design by transforming analog prototypes (bilinear transform) such as Butterworth or Chebyshev.
layers.expert: Bilinear s=(2/T)(1−z⁻¹)/(1+z⁻¹) warps frequency; biquad cascades reduce coefficient sensitivity; limit cycles.

layers.basics: Cutting a signal abruptly smears its spectrum; tapering with a window reduces the smear.
layers.deeper: Hann, Hamming, Blackman trade main-lobe width against side-lobe level.
layers.expert: Rectangular −13 dB sidelobes; Hamming −43 dB; Kaiser window β controls the trade-off.

layers.basics: Decimation lowers the sample rate (after filtering); interpolation raises it (inserting zeros then filtering).
layers.deeper: Saves computation when only a narrow band matters; sample-rate converters in audio.
layers.expert: Polyphase structures; CIC filters in sigma-delta and digital radios; noble identities.

title: Quantization effects
summary: The cost of finite word length.

layers.basics: Rounding to a finite number of bits adds noise and, in filters, can produce small oscillations.
layers.deeper: Quantisation noise power Δ²/12; coefficient rounding shifts poles.
layers.expert: SQNR=6.02B+1.76 dB; dither linearises; noise shaping in sigma-delta; overflow handling (saturate vs wrap).

layers.basics: Fixed-point is cheaper and faster on small chips; floating-point handles a huge range automatically.
layers.deeper: Choose Q-format and scaling to avoid overflow; floats cost more power.
layers.expert: IEEE-754 binary32: 24-bit significand, 8-bit exponent; bfloat16 and int8 for ML accelerators.

title: DSP applications: audio, image, radar, communications

layers.basics: DSP powers audio equalisers, noise cancelling, camera pipelines, radar signal processing and software radios.
layers.deeper: Typical blocks: FIR/IIR filters, FFT, correlators, adaptive filters (LMS).
layers.expert: Matched filter maximises SNR; pulse compression; adaptive beamforming; DSP slices in FPGAs, SIMD in CPUs.

ext.title: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to DSP
